subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 4 Music For Theatre
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: A perfect cadence is formed by which progression?
questions.explain: A perfect (authentic) cadence moves from the dominant (V) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: A retardation differs from a suspension in which way?
options: It resolves upward by step rather than downward
questions.explain: A retardation is a suspended note that resolves upward by step, whereas a suspension resolves downward.

questions.q: In a major key, which chord built on the dominant typically functions as the dominant seventh?
options: A diminished seventh chord on the leading note
A minor seventh chord on the supertonic
A major-minor (dominant) seventh chord on scale degree 5
A major seventh chord on the tonic
questions.explain: The dominant seventh is a major-minor seventh chord built on the fifth degree, comprising a major triad plus a minor seventh.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbols '6/4' indicate which inversion of a triad?
questions.explain: A 6/4 figure denotes a second-inversion triad, with the fifth in the bass.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In performance, 'interpretation' refers to...?
options: Transposing the music to a new key
The performer's expressive choices of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation within the score
Playing the notes exactly as printed with no expressive choices
questions.explain: Interpretation is the performer's expressive shaping of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: A sustained dissonance held over a barline
A note that returns to its starting pitch
Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
Approached by leap and left by step
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: A note held against changing harmony
The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
The inversion of a melodic line
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: The music has no fixed pulse
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The fourth steps down to the third
The fourth leaps up to the sixth
The third rises to the fourth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: An interrupted cadence most commonly progresses from which chord to which?
questions.explain: An interrupted (deceptive) cadence moves from V to vi, thwarting the expected resolution to the tonic.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: Augmentation as a melodic device involves which alteration?
options: Restating a theme with shortened note values
Transposing a theme up an octave
Restating a theme with proportionally lengthened note values
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens the rhythmic values of a theme, typically doubling their duration.

questions.q: A Neapolitan sixth chord is a major triad built on which scale degree, usually in first inversion?
questions.explain: The Neapolitan sixth is a major triad on the flattened supertonic (flattened second degree), typically used in first inversion.

questions.q: What characterises a cadential six-four chord?
options: A tonic chord in root position resolving to V
A second-inversion tonic chord on a strong beat resolving to V before the cadence
A dominant chord in third inversion
questions.explain: The cadential 6/4 is a second-inversion tonic chord on an accented beat that delays and decorates the dominant before the cadence.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The use of only one drum
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
A gradual slowing of the pulse
The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
A slow, free and unmetred mood
Silence with only the drone sounding
A return to the opening alap
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: A tonic pedal is best described as which device?
options: A rapid alternation of tonic and dominant
A modulation to the tonic minor
A melodic ornament on the tonic
A sustained tonic note held while harmonies change above it
questions.explain: A pedal is a sustained or repeated note, the tonic pedal holding the tonic while other parts move through changing harmonies.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: A plagal cadence consists of which progression?
questions.explain: The plagal ('Amen') cadence moves from the subdominant (IV) to the tonic (I).

questions.q: An atonal passage is best characterised by which feature?
options: A clear tonic and dominant relationship
The absence of a tonal centre or key
Strict adherence to a major scale
questions.explain: Atonality avoids any sense of a key or tonal centre, abandoning functional harmony.

questions.q: Which key signature has four sharps?
questions.explain: E major has four sharps: F sharp, C sharp, G sharp and D sharp.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A major piece ending on the minor third
A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A third added above the melody
A chord built on the third degree
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.
